JUDGEMENT CALLS (all five CRITICAL sites inspected in the raw pixels with inkmap, not just the rendered crop)
  S1 (502,355) deg3 - clean T: the column wire rises and terminates on the horizontal rail, which continues both left and right. JUNCTION, not a real choice.

The crossing reading would leave the box top rail carrying only R#7.t0 and R#6.t0, so the two resistors would form a series pair from GND up to a floating midpoint with no source anywhere on it - a currentless dead branch, electrically impossible per rule 1.
  S10 (500,631) deg4 - plain X, same ink character, no dot, no hop. Chose JUNCTION. Crossing would strand the box bottom rail as a 2-terminal floating net (R#7.t1, R#6.t1) and cut both box resistors out of the circuit.
  S11 (358,632) deg3 - T/corner: R#7's bottom lead descends and terminates on the box bottom rail, which continues a short stub left to the box corner (x=345) and right toward S10. JUNCTION.
  S14 (500,706) deg4 - plain X, no dot (dot=2.5, no symmetric blob in the pixel dump), no hop (hop=0.0): the GND column passes straight through the bottom return rail. Chose JUNCTION, so the return rail is net 0. The crossing reading would split off a second rail holding only the V-DC negative terminal and the bottom of L2, whose sole path back to the rest of the circuit is through the series capacitor #0 - the 1V DC source would have no DC return path - and the sheet would carry two distinct 'ground' nets. Rule 1 plus the dataset ink prior (drafters draw a hop when they mean 'not connected') both say junction.
